chapter_text:
CHAPTER 5 — प्राणस्य श्रेष्ठत्वम् (PRANASYA SHRESHTHATVAM)

Introduction — प्राणः कः?

The word प्राण (prana) means the vital breath, the life-force that keeps a living body alive. In the Upanishads the faculties of a human being are grouped as the पञ्च ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि and their inner powers — chiefly वाक् (speech), चक्षुस् (the eye / sight), श्रोत्रम् (the ear / hearing), मनस् (the mind) and प्राणः (the vital breath). This lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) retells, in simple Devanagari Sanskrit prose, the famous Upanishadic dialogue known as प्राण-संवादः or प्राण-विद्या, found in the छान्दोग्य and बृहदारण्यक Upanishads. In this story the vital breath (प्राण) proves that it is श्रेष्ठ (the greatest) among all the faculties, because when it departs the body cannot function at all, while the body can still survive — though poorly — if any of the others leaves. The chapter teaches two great ideas: (1) प्राण is chief because life itself depends on it; and (2) all the faculties must cooperate, for each has its own work and none can do the work of another.

Why this lesson matters (अस्य पाठस्य महत्त्वम्)

Ancient Indian thinkers observed the body closely. They saw that a person can live blind, deaf, mute or even confused in mind — but the moment breathing stops, life ends. From this simple truth they drew a spiritual and a practical lesson. Spiritually, प्राण is honoured as the very support of life, close to the आत्मा (self). Practically, the story teaches humility and teamwork: the eye must not boast that it is greater than the ear, nor speech greater than the mind, for each depends on the others and all depend on प्राण. This is a lesson in सहकार्यम् (cooperation) that applies equally to a family, a classroom and a nation.

The narrative — प्राण-संवादः (with शब्दार्थ and translation)

मूलकथा (simple Sanskrit prose):

पुरा किल इन्द्रियाणि परस्परम् अविवदन्त। वाक् चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनः प्राणश्च — एतानि सर्वाणि "अहं श्रेष्ठः, अहं श्रेष्ठः" इति अवदन्। तेषां विवादः न शाम्यति स्म। ततः तानि सर्वाणि प्रजापतिं पितरम् उपगम्य अपृच्छन् — "भगवन्, अस्माकं मध्ये कः श्रेष्ठः?" इति।
प्रजापतिः अवदत् — "यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते इदं शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव मन्यते, स एव युष्माकं श्रेष्ठः" इति।

शब्दार्थ: पुरा = long ago; किल = it is said; इन्द्रियाणि = the faculties/senses; परस्परम् = with one another; अविवदन्त = disputed; वाक् = speech; चक्षुः = the eye; श्रोत्रम् = the ear; मनः = the mind; प्राणः = the vital breath; अहं श्रेष्ठः = "I am the greatest"; अवदन् = they said; विवादः = the dispute; न शाम्यति स्म = did not cease; प्रजापतिम् = to Prajapati (the father-creator); उपगम्य = having approached; अपृच्छन् = they asked; अस्माकं मध्ये = among us; कः श्रेष्ठः = who is the greatest; यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते = on whose departure; शरीरम् = the body; पापिष्ठतरम् इव = as if in the worst state; मन्यते = seems, is considered; स एव = he alone.
Translation: Long ago the faculties disputed with one another. Speech, the eye, the ear, the mind and the vital breath each declared, "I am the greatest, I am the greatest." Their quarrel would not cease. So they all approached Prajapati, their father, and asked, "Lord, who among us is the greatest?" Prajapati replied, "That one on whose departure the body seems to be in the worst state — he alone is the greatest among you."

The test of departure (उत्क्रमण-परीक्षा):

अथ वाक् उदक्रामत्। सा संवत्सरं प्रोष्य प्रत्यागत्य अपृच्छत् — "कथम् अशकत यूयं मया विना जीवितुम्?" इति। तानि अवदन् — "यथा मूकाः अवदन्तः वाचा, प्राणन्तः प्राणेन, पश्यन्तः चक्षुषा, शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण, ध्यायन्तः मनसा — एवम् अजीविष्म" इति। ततः वाक् पुनः प्राविशत्।
एवमेव चक्षुः उदक्रामत्; तानि अन्धाः इव अजीवन्। श्रोत्रम् उदक्रामत्; तानि बधिराः इव अजीवन्। मनः उदक्रामत्; तानि बालाः इव अजीवन्। किन्तु सर्वेषु एतेषु उत्क्रान्तेषु अपि शरीरं न म्रियते स्म — जीवति स्म एव।

शब्दार्थ: अथ = then; उदक्रामत् = departed (went up/out); संवत्सरम् = for a year; प्रोष्य = having stayed away; प्रत्यागत्य = having returned; कथम् अशकत = how were you able; मया विना = without me; जीवितुम् = to live; मूकाः इव = like mute persons; अवदन्तः वाचा = not speaking with speech; प्राणन्तः प्राणेन = breathing with the breath; पश्यन्तः चक्षुषा = seeing with the eye; शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण = hearing with the ear; ध्यायन्तः मनसा = thinking with the mind; अजीविष्म = we lived; पुनः प्राविशत् = re-entered; अन्धाः इव = like blind persons; बधिराः इव = like deaf persons; बालाः इव = like foolish children; उत्क्रान्तेषु अपि = even when (they) had departed; न म्रियते स्म = did not die.
Translation: Then Speech departed. Having stayed away a year, it returned and asked, "How were you able to live without me?" They answered, "We lived like mute people — not speaking with speech, yet breathing with the breath, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear and thinking with the mind." So Speech entered again. In the same way the eye departed, and they lived like the blind; the ear departed, and they lived like the deaf; the mind departed, and they lived like little children. But even when each of these had gone, the body did not die — it went on living.

The supremacy of प्राण (प्राणस्य श्रेष्ठत्वम्):

अथ प्राणः उत्क्रमिष्यन् आसीत्। स यथा सुहयः पड्वीशशङ्कून् सम्खिदेत्, एवं स इतराणि इन्द्रियाणि सम्खिदति स्म। तानि सर्वाणि व्याकुलानि अभवन्, शरीरं च शिथिलम् अभवत्। ततः तानि सर्वाणि प्राणम् अभिसमेत्य अब्रुवन् — "भगवन्, तिष्ठ, त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः, मा उत्क्रमीः" इति। तानि प्राणं महिम्ना अपूजयन्।

शब्दार्थ: उत्क्रमिष्यन् आसीत् = was about to depart; सुहयः = a fine/good horse; पड्वीश-शङ्कून् = the tethering pegs (to which a horse is tied); सम्खिदेत् = would pull up / tear out; इतराणि इन्द्रियाणि = the other faculties; सम्खिदति स्म = uprooted (pulled along); व्याकुलानि अभवन् = became agitated; शिथिलम् अभवत् = became weak/limp; अभिसमेत्य = having gathered around; अब्रुवन् = said; तिष्ठ = stay!; त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः = you alone are our greatest; मा उत्क्रमीः = do not depart; महिम्ना अपूजयन् = honoured with (words of) greatness.
Translation: Then the vital breath was about to depart. Just as a fine horse, when it starts, tears up the very pegs to which it is tethered, so the breath, as it rose to leave, pulled up all the other faculties with it. They all became agitated and the body grew limp. Then they all gathered around the breath and said, "Lord, stay! You alone are the greatest among us — do not depart." And they honoured the breath with words of its greatness.

The moral (उपदेशः):

अस्याः कथायाः द्वौ उपदेशौ। प्रथमः — प्राणः श्रेष्ठः, यतः तस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं म्रियते, अन्येषु तु उत्क्रान्तेषु शरीरं जीवति एव। द्वितीयः — सर्वाणि इन्द्रियाणि परस्परं सहकार्यं कुर्युः; न कश्चित् एकः "अहम् एव श्रेष्ठः" इति गर्वं कुर्यात्, यतः प्रत्येकस्य स्वं कार्यम् अस्ति, प्राणश्च सर्वेषाम् आधारः।
Moral: The story carries two lessons. First, प्राण (the breath) is supreme, for when it leaves, the body dies, whereas when the others leave the body still lives. Second, all the faculties should cooperate; no single one should be proud and say "I alone am the greatest," because each has its own work, and प्राण is the support of them all — just as in a family or a team every member matters, yet all depend on one shared life.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the lesson (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds).
  • प्राणः + च → प्राणश्च (विसर्ग-सन्धि: visarga ः before च becomes श्). Split back: प्राणः + च.
  • इति + अवदत् → इत्यवदत् (यण्-सन्धि: इ + अ = य्). Split back: इति + अवदत्.
  • न + अस्ति → नास्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धि: अ + अ = आ). Split back: न + अस्ति.
  • तथा + एव → तथैव (वृद्धि-सन्धि: आ + ए = ऐ). Split back: तथा + एव.
  • उत् + क्रान्तः → उत्क्रान्तः (व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). Split back: उत् + क्रान्तः.
  • स + एव → स एव (kept separate here for clarity). Being able to SPLIT a sandhi (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Using the masculine a-stem प्राण as a model where useful:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, the subject): प्राणः "the breath (does)". In the story वाक्, चक्षुः, प्राणः are subjects.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, the object): प्राणम् "(they honoured) the breath"; प्रजापतिम् "(they approached) Prajapati".
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): प्राणेन "with the breath", चक्षुषा "with the eye", मनसा "with the mind".
  • चतुर्थी / पञ्चमी: पञ्चमी (ablative, "from") — e.g. शरीरात् "from the body".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): इन्द्रियाणाम् "of the faculties", अस्माकम् "of us".
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at/on"): शरीरे "in the body", यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते "on whose departure" (a सति-सप्तमी / locative-absolute).

(C) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The word प्राण (masculine, a-stem) in the प्रथमा (nominative): एकवचन प्राणः (one breath), द्विवचन प्राणौ (two), बहुवचन प्राणाः (many/the vital breaths). Notice the neuter plural इन्द्रियाणि (faculties) and सर्वाणि (all) are प्रथमा/द्वितीया बहुवचन of neuter a-stems, ending in -आणि.

(D) धातुरूप (conjugation — worked example). The root √वद् (to speak), परस्मैपद, लट्-लकार (present tense): प्रथमपुरुष वदति / वदतः / वदन्ति; मध्यमपुरुष वदसि / वदथः / वदथ; उत्तमपुरुष वदामि / वदावः / वदामः. Also √अस् (to be), लट्: अस्ति / स्तः / सन्ति. In the story we meet related past forms such as अवदन् (they said, लङ्) and उदक्रामत् (it departed, लङ् of उद्+क्रम्).

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you read the Upanishadic प्राण-संवाद — the dialogue in which speech, the eye, the ear, the mind and the vital breath quarrel over who is greatest. Prajapati sets the test: the greatest is the one whose departure leaves the body worst off. One by one the faculties leave for a year; the body survives as a mute, a blind man, a deaf man and a simpleton — but survives. When प्राण alone begins to leave, it uproots all the others like a horse tearing up its tethering pegs, and they beg it to stay, honouring it as श्रेष्ठ. The two lessons are that प्राण is chief because life depends on it, and that the faculties must cooperate humbly, each doing its own work. You also learned grammar from the passage: सन्धि joins and splits (प्राणश्च, इत्यवदत्, नास्ति, तथैव), the six विभक्ति case-endings with examples (प्राणः, प्राणम्, प्राणेन, इन्द्रियाणाम्, शरीरे), a शब्दरूप model (प्राणः / प्राणौ / प्राणाः) and a धातुरूप model (वदति / वदतः / वदन्ति). Recite the moral often: honour the life-breath, and let every faculty work together.

sections.heading: The setting of the dialogue
bullets: The story comes from the छान्दोग्य and बृहदारण्यक Upanishads and is called प्राण-संवाद or प्राण-विद्या.
Five faculties — वाक् (speech), चक्षुस् (eye), श्रोत्रम् (ear), मनस् (mind) and प्राणः (breath) — dispute, each saying 'अहं श्रेष्ठः' (I am the greatest).
Unable to settle the quarrel, they approach प्रजापति, who sets a fair test to decide the greatest.

sections.heading: The test of departure and its result
bullets: प्रजापति's rule: the greatest is the one on whose departure the body seems worst off (पापिष्ठतरम् इव).
Speech leaves — the body lives like a mute; the eye leaves — like the blind; the ear — like the deaf; the mind — like a simpleton; yet it survives.
When प्राण begins to leave, it uproots all the other faculties, just as a fine horse tears up the pegs to which it is tied.
The others beg प्राण to stay ('मा उत्क्रमीः') and honour it as the greatest.

sections.heading: The moral — cooperation and humility
bullets: प्राण is supreme because life itself depends on it — without breath the body dies.
No faculty should be proud; each has its own work and cannot do another's.
The faculties must cooperate (सहकार्यम्), just as members of a family or team depend on one another and on a shared life.

sections.heading: Sandhi from the passage
bullets: विसर्ग-सन्धि: प्राणः + च = प्राणश्च (ः → श् before च).
यण्-सन्धि: इति + अवदत् = इत्यवदत् (इ + अ = य्).
दीर्घ-सन्धि: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ); वृद्धि-सन्धि: तथा + एव = तथैव (आ + ए = ऐ).
सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting a joined form back into its words) is a key reading skill.

sections.heading: Vibhakti, shabda-rupa and dhatu-rupa
bullets: विभक्ति: प्रथमा प्राणः (subject), द्वितीया प्राणम् (object), तृतीया प्राणेन (by/with), षष्ठी इन्द्रियाणाम् (of), सप्तमी शरीरे (in).
शब्दरूप of a-stem प्राण (प्रथमा): एकवचन प्राणः, द्विवचन प्राणौ, बहुवचन प्राणाः.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — प्राणस्य श्रेष्ठत्वम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 5)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the प्राण-संवाद passage in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Who are the faculties that dispute in the प्राण-संवाद, and what does each claim? / प्राण-संवादे कानि इन्द्रियाणि विवदन्ते, प्रत्येकं किम् अवदत्?
questions.answer: The disputing faculties are वाक् (speech), चक्षुः (the eye), श्रोत्रम् (the ear), मनः (the mind) and प्राणः (the vital breath). Each one claims 'अहं श्रेष्ठः' — 'I am the greatest'.
questions.explanation: The five faculties each boast of being श्रेष्ठ, which starts the dispute.

questions.question: What test did प्रजापति set to decide who is greatest? / श्रेष्ठत्व-निर्णयाय प्रजापतिः कां परीक्षाम् अकरोत्?
questions.answer: प्रजापति said that the greatest is the one on whose departure the body seems to be in the worst state — 'यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते इदं शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव मन्यते, स एव श्रेष्ठः'. So each faculty had to leave the body for a year and see how the body fared.
questions.explanation: The test is the effect of each faculty's departure (उत्क्रमण) on the body.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each: उत्क्रान्ते, चक्षुषा, मनसा, श्रेष्ठः, प्राणेन.
questions.answer: उत्क्रान्ते = on (its) departure; चक्षुषा = with the eye; मनसा = with the mind; श्रेष्ठः = greatest/best; प्राणेन = with the breath.
questions.explanation: चक्षुषा, मनसा, प्राणेन are तृतीया (instrumental) 'with/by' forms from the passage.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) प्राणश्च (b) इत्यवदत् (c) नास्ति.
questions.answer: (a) प्राणश्च = प्राणः + च (विसर्ग-सन्धि, ः → श् before च). (b) इत्यवदत् = इति + अवदत् (यण्-सन्धि, इ + अ = य्). (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धि, अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its role for each word: प्राणम्, प्राणेन, शरीरे.
questions.answer: प्राणम् = द्वितीया (accusative), the object → '(they honoured) the breath'. प्राणेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'with/by the breath'. शरीरे = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in the body'.
questions.explanation: द्वितीया marks the object, तृतीया the means, सप्तमी the place.

questions.question: Explain how प्राण proves that it is श्रेष्ठ, including the simile of the horse. / प्राणः कथं स्वस्य श्रेष्ठत्वं प्रमाणयति — अश्वस्य उदाहरणसहितं लिखत।
questions.answer: When speech, the eye, the ear and the mind each departed for a year, the body survived — living like a mute, a blind man, a deaf man and a simpleton, but it did not die. But when प्राण (the breath) was about to depart, it began to uproot all the other faculties along with it, just as a fine horse (सुहयः), when it starts, tears up the very pegs (पड्वीश-शङ्कून्) to which it is tethered. The body grew limp and the faculties became agitated. Seeing that they could not survive its departure, they all gathered around प्राण and begged, 'तिष्ठ, मा उत्क्रमीः' — stay, do not depart — and honoured it as the greatest. This proves प्राण श्रेष्ठ, because life itself depends on it: when the others leave the body still lives, but when प्राण leaves the body dies.
questions.explanation: The horse-and-pegs simile shows प्राण dragging all faculties with it; life depends on breath alone.

questions.question: What is the moral of the प्राण-संवाद, and how can a student practise it today? / प्राण-संवादस्य उपदेशः कः, छात्रः तम् अद्य कथम् आचरेत्?
questions.answer: The story teaches two lessons. First, प्राण is supreme because life depends on it — so we should respect and care for our health and breath (through calm breathing, good habits and प्राणायाम). Second, and more broadly, it teaches सहकार्यम् (cooperation) and humility: just as the eye, ear, speech and mind each have their own work and none can do another's, so no one should be proud and think 'I alone am the greatest'. A student can practise this by working together in a team, respecting every classmate's contribution, not boasting, and understanding that a class, family or nation succeeds only when each member does their own part while depending on the others. Pride divides; cooperation, supported by a shared purpose (like प्राण in the body), keeps the whole alive and strong.
questions.explanation: Two morals: reverence for the life-breath, and cooperation/humility among interdependent parts.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते इदं शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव मन्यते, स एव श्रेष्ठः।'
questions.answer: 'That one on whose departure this body seems to be in the worst state — he alone is the greatest.' This is प्रजापति's rule for deciding which faculty is श्रेष्ठ.
questions.explanation: यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते is a locative-absolute ('on the departure of whom'); स एव = he alone.

questions.question: How did the body live when the eye, the ear and the mind departed one by one? / चक्षुषि श्रोत्रे मनसि च क्रमेण उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं कथम् अजीवत्?
questions.answer: When the eye departed the body lived like a blind person (अन्धः इव); when the ear departed, like a deaf person (बधिरः इव); when the mind departed, like a simpleton/child (बालः इव). In each case the body was worse off but still survived.
questions.explanation: Each departure leaves a specific handicap, but not death — unlike प्राण.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (present tense, परस्मैपद) of √वद् in all three persons (singular). / वद्-धातोः लट्-लकारे एकवचने त्रीणि रूपाणि लिखत।
questions.answer: प्रथमपुरुष (3rd) वदति ('he/she/it speaks'); मध्यमपुरुष (2nd) वदसि ('you speak'); उत्तमपुरुष (1st) वदामि ('I speak').
questions.explanation: √वद् is an a-conjugation (भ्वादि) परस्मैपद verb; singular present forms are वदति / वदसि / वदामि.

questions.question: प्राण's departure is compared to a horse tearing up its tethering pegs. / प्राणस्य उत्क्रमणं अश्वस्य शङ्कु-उत्खननेन उपमितम्।
questions.explanation: सुहयः पड्वीश-शङ्कून् सम्खिदेत् — the horse simile.

questions.question: The story teaches that one faculty can do the work of all the others. / एकम् इन्द्रियं सर्वेषां कार्यं कर्तुं शक्नोति इति कथा शिक्षयति।
questions.explanation: Each faculty has its own work; none can do another's — hence cooperation.

questions.question: 'मूकः' means a mute person (one who cannot speak). / 'मूकः' इति अवाक् जनः।
questions.explanation: मूकः = mute.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नास्ति' is न + अस्ति. / 'नास्ति' इत्यस्य विच्छेदः न + अस्ति।
questions.explanation: दीर्घ-सन्धि: अ + अ = आ.

questions.question: In 'प्राणेन', the word is in the तृतीया (instrumental) case. / 'प्राणेन' इति तृतीया-विभक्तौ अस्ति।
questions.explanation: -एन = तृतीया एकवचन.

questions.question: When the mind departed, the body lived like a simpleton/child. / मनसि उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं बालः इव अजीवत्।
questions.explanation: Without मनस् the body lived like a बाल.

questions.question: Each faculty left the body for a year as part of the test. / परीक्षायां प्रत्येकम् इन्द्रियं संवत्सरं शरीरात् अगच्छत्।
questions.explanation: Each departed संवत्सरम् (for a year).

questions.question: The vital breath is called ____ in Sanskrit. / संस्कृते जीवनवायुः ____ इति कथ्यते।
questions.explanation: प्राणः = the vital breath.

questions.question: The faculties asked ____ to decide who was greatest. / इन्द्रियाणि ____ अपृच्छन् कः श्रेष्ठः इति।
questions.explanation: They asked प्रजापति (प्रजापतिम्, द्वितीया).

questions.question: Without speech (वाक्) the body lived like a ____. / वाचि उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं ____ इव अजीवत्।
questions.explanation: Without वाक् the body is like a mute (मूकः).

questions.question: Without the eye the body lived like an ____. / चक्षुषि उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं ____ इव अजीवत्।
questions.explanation: Without चक्षुस् the body is like the blind (अन्धः).

questions.question: Without the ear the body lived like a ____. / श्रोत्रे उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं ____ इव अजीवत्।
questions.explanation: Without श्रोत्रम् the body is like the deaf (बधिरः).

questions.question: प्राण's departure is compared to a ____ tearing up its tethering pegs. / प्राणस्य उत्क्रमणं ____ शङ्कु-उत्खननेन उपमितम्।
questions.explanation: सुहयः (a fine horse) tears up its pegs.

questions.question: The faculties begged प्राण, 'तिष्ठ, मा ____' (do not depart). / इन्द्रियाणि प्राणम् अवदन् 'तिष्ठ, मा ____'।
questions.explanation: मा उत्क्रमीः = do not depart.

questions.question: सन्धि: प्राणः + च = ____.
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धि: ः → श् before च.

questions.question: सन्धि: इति + अवदत् = ____.
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धि: इ + अ = य्.

questions.question: सन्धि: न + अस्ति = ____.
questions.explanation: दीर्घ-सन्धि: अ + अ = आ.

questions.question: The प्रथमा (nom.) singular शब्दरूप of प्राण is ____.
questions.explanation: प्रथमा एकवचन = प्राणः.

questions.question: The present-tense 3rd-person singular form of √वद् is ____.
questions.explanation: लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचन = वदति.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'संवत्सरम्' means for a ____. / 'संवत्सरम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः एकं ____।
questions.explanation: संवत्सरम् = for a year (वर्षम्).

questions.question: The moral of the story is ____ (working together). / कथायाः उपदेशः ____ अस्ति।
questions.explanation: सहकार्यम् = cooperation.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'श्रेष्ठः' means ____. / 'श्रेष्ठः' इत्यस्य अर्थः ____।
questions.explanation: श्रेष्ठः = greatest / best.

questions.question: Name the five faculties that dispute in the प्राण-संवाद. / प्राण-संवादे कानि पञ्च इन्द्रियाणि विवदन्ते?
questions.answer: The five faculties are वाक् (speech), चक्षुः (the eye), श्रोत्रम् (the ear), मनः (the mind) and प्राणः (the vital breath).
questions.explanation: These five each claim to be greatest.

questions.question: Why did the faculties go to प्रजापति? / इन्द्रियाणि किमर्थं प्रजापतिम् अगच्छन्?
questions.answer: Because their dispute over who was greatest ('अहं श्रेष्ठः') could not be settled among themselves, they went to प्रजापति, their father, to judge who was truly श्रेष्ठ.
questions.explanation: An outside judge was needed to end the quarrel.

questions.question: State प्रजापति's rule for deciding the greatest. / श्रेष्ठत्व-निर्णयस्य नियमः कः?
questions.answer: प्रजापति said: the greatest is the one on whose departure the body seems worst off — 'यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव मन्यते, स एव श्रेष्ठः'.
questions.explanation: The test is the effect of departure on the body.

questions.question: State the function of प्राण and one other faculty. / प्राणस्य अन्यस्य च एकस्य इन्द्रियस्य कार्यं लिखत।
questions.answer: प्राणः keeps the body alive (it is the vital breath). वाक् (speech) enables speaking; चक्षुस् enables seeing; श्रोत्रम् enables hearing; मनस् enables thinking (any one is acceptable).
questions.explanation: Each faculty has a distinct कार्य.

questions.question: Explain what happened when प्राण began to depart. / प्राणे उत्क्रमितुम् आरब्धे किम् अभवत्?
questions.answer: As प्राण rose to leave, it began to uproot all the other faculties along with it, just as a fine horse tears up the pegs to which it is tethered. The body grew limp and the faculties became agitated, so they all begged प्राण to stay.
questions.explanation: प्राण's departure drags the others out — showing life depends on it.

questions.question: What is the moral of the प्राण-संवाद? / प्राण-संवादस्य उपदेशः कः?
questions.answer: Two lessons: (1) प्राण is supreme because life depends on it; without breath the body dies. (2) The faculties must cooperate (सहकार्यम्) with humility — each has its own work, none can do another's, and all depend on प्राण. Pride ('I alone am greatest') is wrong.
questions.explanation: Supremacy of प्राण plus cooperation/humility.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: मूकः, अन्धः, बधिरः, बालः.
questions.answer: मूकः = mute (cannot speak); अन्धः = blind; बधिरः = deaf; बालः = a child / simpleton.
questions.explanation: These describe the body when speech, eye, ear or mind departs.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: इन्द्रियाणि, उत्क्रान्ते, सुहयः, संवत्सरम्.
questions.answer: इन्द्रियाणि = the faculties/senses; उत्क्रान्ते = on (its) departure; सुहयः = a fine horse; संवत्सरम् = for a year.
questions.explanation: Key vocabulary from the passage.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) इत्यवदत् (b) तथैव.
questions.answer: (a) इत्यवदत् = इति + अवदत् (यण्-सन्धि, इ + अ = य्). (b) तथैव = तथा + एव (वृद्धि-सन्धि, आ + ए = ऐ).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: Name the सन्धि type in each: प्राणश्च, नास्ति.
questions.answer: प्राणश्च = विसर्ग-सन्धि (ः → श् before च). नास्ति = दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Identify the rule that produces each join.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and role of: प्राणम्, इन्द्रियाणाम्.
questions.answer: प्राणम् = द्वितीया (accusative), the object → '(they honoured) the breath'. इन्द्रियाणाम् = षष्ठी बहुवचन (genitive plural) → 'of the faculties'.
questions.explanation: द्वितीया marks the object; षष्ठी marks 'of'.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of प्राण (प्रथमा) in all three numbers. / प्राण-शब्दस्य प्रथमा-विभक्तौ त्रीणि वचनानि लिखत।
questions.answer: एकवचन प्राणः (one), द्विवचन प्राणौ (two), बहुवचन प्राणाः (many) — the प्रथमा (nominative) of the a-stem noun प्राण.
questions.explanation: a-stem masculine प्रथमा: -ः / -औ / -आः.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'तानि सर्वाणि प्राणम् अभिसमेत्य अब्रुवन् — तिष्ठ, त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः।'
questions.answer: 'All of them gathered around the breath and said: Stay! You alone are our greatest.' The faculties beg प्राण not to depart and honour it as chief.
questions.explanation: अभिसमेत्य = having gathered around; त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः = you alone are our greatest.

questions.question: Translate: 'अहं श्रेष्ठः, अहं श्रेष्ठः' इति प्रत्येकम् अवदत्.
questions.answer: 'I am the greatest, I am the greatest' — thus each one said. This shows how the dispute began, with every faculty boasting.
questions.explanation: प्रत्येकम् = each one; अवदत् = said.

questions.question: Read: 'चक्षुषि उत्क्रान्ते तानि अन्धाः इव अजीवन्।' Translate and say what it shows.
questions.answer: Translation: 'When the eye had departed, they lived like the blind.' It shows that the body survives without sight — merely handicapped, not dead — unlike when प्राण departs.
questions.explanation: A locative-absolute (चक्षुषि उत्क्रान्ते) plus the point that the body still lives.

questions.question: Why did the body not die when speech, eye, ear or mind departed? / वाचि चक्षुषि श्रोत्रे मनसि वा उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं किमर्थं न अम्रियत?
questions.answer: Because none of these is the life-force itself: while one was gone, the body still breathed with प्राण, and used the remaining faculties. It was only handicapped (mute, blind, deaf or simple), not lifeless — showing प्राण, not they, sustains life.
questions.explanation: Life rests on प्राण, so losing other faculties only handicaps the body.

questions.question: Give one example of applying सहकार्यम् in daily life. / दैनन्दिनजीवने सहकार्यस्य एकम् उदाहरणं लिखत।
questions.answer: Example: in a group project or at home, each person does their own task (one cooks, one cleans, one studies) and respects the others, so the whole family or team succeeds together — just as the faculties cooperate under प्राण.
questions.explanation: Any teamwork example showing interdependence and humility is acceptable.

questions.question: How does the horse simile prove प्राण's supremacy? / अश्व-उदाहरणेन प्राणस्य श्रेष्ठत्वं कथं सिध्यति?
questions.answer: A tethered horse, when it starts to move, pulls up the very pegs it is tied to. Likewise प्राण, when it starts to leave, drags all the other faculties out with it and the body collapses. Since the other faculties cannot remain (or the body cannot live) once प्राण goes, प्राण is shown to be their support and therefore श्रेष्ठ.
questions.explanation: The simile shows all faculties are 'tied' to प्राण and leave with it.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: चक्षुषा, मनसा, प्राणेन.
questions.answer: चक्षुषा = with the eye; मनसा = with the mind; प्राणेन = with the breath. All three are तृतीया (instrumental) 'with/by' forms.
questions.explanation: These -आ/-एन endings mark the तृतीया case.

questions.question: In one sentence, describe the setting of the story. / एकवाक्ये कथायाः प्रसङ्गं वर्णयत।
questions.answer: Long ago the faculties — speech, eye, ear, mind and breath — quarrelled over who was greatest and went to प्रजापति to decide.
questions.explanation: A one-line summary of the opening संवाद.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप of √वद् (present) in the three persons singular. / वद्-धातोः लट्-लकारे एकवचने त्रीणि रूपाणि लिखत।
questions.answer: वदति (3rd, he/she/it speaks), वदसि (2nd, you speak), वदामि (1st, I speak).
questions.explanation: √वद्, परस्मैपद, लट्, एकवचन.

questions.question: Translate: 'प्राणे उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं न जीवति।' and give the point it makes.
questions.answer: 'When the breath has departed, the body does not live.' This is the crux of the lesson: unlike the other faculties, प्राण's departure ends life — so प्राण is श्रेष्ठ.
questions.explanation: A locative-absolute stating why प्राण is supreme.

questions.question: Retell the प्राण-संवाद story in your own simple words (5-6 sentences). / प्राण-संवादस्य कथां स्वशब्दैः लिखत।
questions.answer: Long ago the faculties — speech, the eye, the ear, the mind and the vital breath — quarrelled, each saying 'I am the greatest'. Unable to settle it, they went to प्रजापति, who said the greatest is the one whose departure leaves the body worst off. One by one, speech, the eye, the ear and the mind left for a year; the body lived as a mute, a blind man, a deaf man and a simpleton, but it survived. Finally, when the breath (प्राण) began to leave, it uprooted all the other faculties, just as a horse tears up its tethering pegs. The body grew limp, so the others begged प्राण to stay and honoured it as श्रेष्ठ. Thus प्राण was proved to be the greatest faculty.
questions.explanation: A complete retelling: dispute, test, departures, प्राण's uprooting, conclusion.

questions.question: Explain in detail why प्राण is called श्रेष्ठ, contrasting its departure with the others'. / प्राणः किमर्थं श्रेष्ठः — अन्येषाम् उत्क्रमणेन सह तुलयित्वा विस्तरेण लिखत।
questions.answer: When speech departed, the body lived like a mute; when the eye departed, like the blind; when the ear departed, like the deaf; when the mind departed, like a simpleton. In every case the body was worse off but still alive, because it went on breathing with प्राण and using the remaining faculties. But when प्राण itself began to depart, it dragged all the other faculties out with it — like a fine horse tearing up the pegs to which it is tethered — and the body grew limp and lifeless. The others, unable to survive its loss, gathered around प्राण and begged it to stay, honouring it as the greatest. The contrast is clear: the loss of any other faculty only handicaps the body, but the loss of प्राण ends life. Because life itself depends on प्राण and all the faculties depend on it, प्राण is श्रेष्ठ.
questions.explanation: Point-by-point contrast: handicap vs death; the horse simile; life depends on प्राण.

questions.question: What does the प्राण-संवाद teach about cooperation and pride? Apply it to school life. / प्राण-संवादः सहकार्यविषये गर्वविषये च किं शिक्षयति? विद्यालयजीवने योजयत।
questions.answer: The story begins with pride: each faculty boasts 'I alone am the greatest', and the quarrel harms them all. The test reveals the truth — every faculty has its own work and none can do another's, and all depend on प्राण, the shared life. So the real teaching is सहकार्यम् (cooperation) and humility: greatness lies not in boasting but in doing one's own part while respecting others. In school, this means students, teachers and staff each have their role — one studies, one teaches, one keeps the school clean — and the school flourishes only when all cooperate humbly, as the faculties do under प्राण. Pride divides and weakens a group; cooperation, resting on a shared purpose, keeps it alive and strong. A wise student therefore avoids boasting, values every classmate's contribution, and works as part of a team.
questions.explanation: Evaluate the pride-vs-cooperation theme and apply it concretely to school.

questions.question: Describe the function of each faculty and the condition of the body when it departs. / प्रत्येकस्य इन्द्रियस्य कार्यं तस्य उत्क्रमणे च शरीरस्य अवस्थां वर्णयत।
questions.answer: वाक् (speech) lets one speak; without it the body lives like a mute (मूकः). चक्षुस् (the eye) lets one see; without it the body lives like the blind (अन्धः). श्रोत्रम् (the ear) lets one hear; without it the body lives like the deaf (बधिरः). मनस् (the mind) lets one think; without it the body lives like a simpleton (बालः). प्राणः (the breath) keeps the body alive; without it the body cannot live at all and dies. Thus the first four only handicap the body when they leave, but प्राण alone is essential to life.
questions.explanation: Function + resulting condition for each of the five faculties.

questions.question: Take four सन्धि examples from the lesson, join and split each, and name the सन्धि. / पाठात् चत्वारि सन्धि-उदाहरणानि गृहीत्वा सन्धिं विच्छेदं च कुरुत।
questions.answer: 1) प्राणः + च = प्राणश्च — विसर्ग-सन्धि (ः → श् before च); split: प्राणः + च. 2) इति + अवदत् = इत्यवदत् — यण्-सन्धि (इ + अ = य्); split: इति + अवदत्. 3) न + अस्ति = नास्ति — दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ); split: न + अस्ति. 4) तथा + एव = तथैव — वृद्धि-सन्धि (आ + ए = ऐ); split: तथा + एव. Joining is सन्धि; splitting back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
questions.explanation: Four worked सन्धि examples with type and विच्छेद.

questions.question: Explain the six विभक्ति cases with one example each from the lesson. / षट् विभक्तीः पाठात् एकैकम् उदाहरणसहितं वर्णयत।
questions.answer: प्रथमा (subject): प्राणः 'the breath (acts)'. द्वितीया (object): प्राणम् '(they honoured) the breath'. तृतीया (with/by): प्राणेन 'with the breath', चक्षुषा 'with the eye'. पञ्चमी (from): शरीरात् 'from the body'. षष्ठी (of): इन्द्रियाणाम् 'of the faculties'. सप्तमी (in/on): शरीरे 'in the body'. Each ending signals the word's role in the sentence.
questions.explanation: Six cases, each with a lesson example and its role.

questions.question: Translate the following passage into simple English and state its moral: 'यथा सुहयः पड्वीश-शङ्कून् सम्खिदेत्, एवं प्राणः इतराणि इन्द्रियाणि सम्खिदति स्म। ततः तानि प्राणम् अब्रुवन् — तिष्ठ, त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः।'
questions.answer: Translation: 'Just as a fine horse tears up the pegs to which it is tethered, so the breath (प्राण) uprooted the other faculties (as it began to leave). Then they said to the breath: Stay! You alone are our greatest.' Moral: because every faculty is 'tied' to प्राण and cannot survive its departure, प्राण is proved to be the greatest — life itself depends on the breath, and all the faculties must depend on and cooperate with it.
questions.explanation: Translate the horse simile and the plea, then draw the moral of प्राण's supremacy.

questions.question: 'प्राणश्च सर्वेषाम् आधारः।' Explain this idea and why it matters. / एतत् वाक्यं व्याख्यायत तस्य महत्त्वं च लिखत।
questions.answer: 'And प्राण is the support of all.' The line captures the whole lesson: the eye, ear, speech and mind can each work only while the body lives, and the body lives only because of प्राण. So प्राण is the common foundation (आधार) that supports every faculty. This matters because it teaches that in any group — body, family, class or nation — there is some shared support or purpose on which all members depend; recognising it brings humility and cooperation, while forgetting it brings pride and conflict. Honouring the shared support keeps the whole alive and united.
questions.explanation: Explain प्राण as the common आधार and its lesson of humble interdependence.

questions.question: Passage: 'ततः तानि सर्वाणि प्रजापतिं पितरम् उपगम्य अपृच्छन् — भगवन्, अस्माकं मध्ये कः श्रेष्ठः? प्रजापतिः अवदत् — यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव मन्यते, स एव श्रेष्ठः।' Q: Whom did the faculties approach, and what rule did he give?
questions.answer: The faculties approached प्रजापति, their father. He gave the rule that the greatest is the one on whose departure the body seems to be in the worst state ('यस्मिन् उत्क्रान्ते... स एव श्रेष्ठः').
questions.explanation: The passage gives प्रजापति's test for deciding श्रेष्ठत्व.

questions.question: Passage: 'वाक् उदक्रामत्। सा संवत्सरं प्रोष्य प्रत्यागत्य अपृच्छत् — कथम् अशकत यूयं मया विना जीवितुम्? तानि अवदन् — यथा मूकाः, एवम् अजीविष्म।' Q: What happened when वाक् departed, and how did the body live?
questions.answer: Speech (वाक्) departed and stayed away for a year. On returning it asked how they had lived without it. They replied that they had lived like mute people (मूकाः) — unable to speak, but still breathing, seeing, hearing and thinking. So वाक् entered again.
questions.explanation: The body survives वाक्'s loss, living like a mute.

questions.question: Passage: 'अथ प्राणः उत्क्रमिष्यन् आसीत्। स यथा सुहयः पड्वीश-शङ्कून् सम्खिदेत्, एवं इतराणि इन्द्रियाणि सम्खिदति स्म। तानि व्याकुलानि अभवन्।' Q: What did प्राण do as it began to leave, and what does the horse simile mean?
questions.answer: As प्राण began to leave, it uprooted all the other faculties along with it, and they became agitated. The horse simile means that just as a tethered horse tears up its pegs when it starts to move, प्राण, on leaving, drags out all the faculties tied to it — showing that they cannot remain (and the body cannot live) without प्राण.
questions.explanation: The simile shows all faculties depend on प्राण; its loss uproots them.

questions.question: Passage: 'तानि सर्वाणि प्राणम् अभिसमेत्य अब्रुवन् — भगवन्, तिष्ठ, त्वम् एव नः श्रेष्ठः, मा उत्क्रमीः। तानि प्राणं महिम्ना अपूजयन्।' Q: What did the faculties finally say to प्राण, and what does this prove?
questions.answer: They gathered around प्राण and begged, 'Lord, stay! You alone are our greatest — do not depart,' and honoured it with words of its greatness. This proves that प्राण is श्रेष्ठ, because the faculties themselves admit they cannot live without it.
questions.explanation: The faculties' own plea confirms प्राण's supremacy.

questions.question: Passage: 'चक्षुः उदक्रामत्; तानि अन्धाः इव अजीवन्। श्रोत्रम् उदक्रामत्; तानि बधिराः इव अजीवन्। मनः उदक्रामत्; तानि बालाः इव अजीवन्।' Q: What does this passage tell us about the eye, ear and mind compared with प्राण?
questions.answer: It tells us that when the eye, ear or mind departs, the body is only handicapped — living like the blind, the deaf or a simpleton — but it still survives. This contrasts with प्राण, whose departure the body cannot survive at all. Hence these three are not the greatest; प्राण is.
questions.explanation: The body survives loss of eye/ear/mind, unlike loss of प्राण.

questions.question: Passage: 'न कश्चित् एकः अहम् एव श्रेष्ठः इति गर्वं कुर्यात्, यतः प्रत्येकस्य स्वं कार्यम् अस्ति, प्राणश्च सर्वेषाम् आधारः।' Q: What lesson about pride and cooperation does this passage give? Give one real-life application.
questions.answer: The passage teaches that no one should be proud and claim to be the greatest alone, because each faculty (or person) has its own work and all depend on a shared support — प्राण in the body. The lesson is humility and cooperation (सहकार्यम्). Real-life application: in a team project each member should do their own task and respect the others, so the whole team succeeds, instead of one person boasting and dividing the group.
questions.explanation: The passage rejects pride and teaches cooperation under a shared support.

questions.question: Passage: 'पुरा किल इन्द्रियाणि परस्परम् अविवदन्त। वाक् चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनः प्राणश्च अहं श्रेष्ठः इति अवदन्।' Q: What is happening in this opening passage?
questions.answer: In the opening, the faculties — speech, the eye, the ear, the mind and the vital breath — are quarrelling with one another, each declaring 'I am the greatest'. This dispute is what begins the whole story.
questions.explanation: The passage sets up the dispute among the five faculties.

questions.question: Passage: 'यथा मूकाः अवदन्तः वाचा, प्राणन्तः प्राणेन, पश्यन्तः चक्षुषा, शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण, ध्यायन्तः मनसा — एवम् अजीविष्म।' Q: List the faculties named here and the action each performs.
questions.answer: The passage names: वाच् (speech) — speaking; प्राण (breath) — breathing; चक्षुस् (eye) — seeing; श्रोत्रम् (ear) — hearing; मनस् (mind) — thinking. It shows that while speech was gone, the body still carried on all the other functions.
questions.explanation: Each faculty is paired with its own action (तृतीया 'with' forms).

questions.question: Passage: 'प्राणश्च... इत्यवदत्... नास्ति... तथैव.' Q: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of प्राणश्च and इत्यवदत्, and name the सन्धि in each.
questions.answer: प्राणश्च = प्राणः + च (विसर्ग-सन्धि: visarga ः becomes श् before च). इत्यवदत् = इति + अवदत् (यण्-सन्धि: इ + अ = य्).
questions.explanation: Two सन्धि splits with their types, drawn from the passage.

questions.question: Passage: 'प्राणः श्रेष्ठः। तानि प्राणम् अपूजयन्। शरीरं प्राणेन जीवति।' Q: Identify the विभक्ति (case) of प्राणः, प्राणम् and प्राणेन, and give the role of each.
questions.answer: प्राणः = प्रथमा (nominative), the subject → 'the breath (is greatest / lives)'. प्राणम् = द्वितीया (accusative), the object → '(they honoured) the breath'. प्राणेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by/with the breath (the body lives)'. The three forms show the same word in subject, object and instrumental roles.
questions.explanation: Same noun प्राण in प्रथमा, द्वितीया and तृतीया with roles.
